mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from its recent trough while TRANSIT stops falling, the commuting base expands and weekday trips to shops and restaurants rise within four weeks, pushing RETAIL_REC above its prior 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -37.3 to -21.9 in the latest week while TRANSIT improved from -38.9 to -31.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-28-day mean for the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RESIDENTIAL from elevated levels signals more time spent outside the home; when RESIDENTIAL falls back below 10 points above baseline, retail visits increase in the following 1-2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10 points above baseline after being at or above 10
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 13.0 at t-1w and 9.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: After RESIDENTIAL crosses below 10 above baseline, RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 4-week average within the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: If transit mobility weakens while workplaces stay suppressed, access friction to downtown retail persists and retail-and-recreation mobility declines over the next four weeks as discretionary trips are postponed.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remained around -32 to -39 and WORKPLACES remained around -22 to -37 across the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT staying below -25 and WORKPLACES staying below -20 for most of that period.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS during colder-season holiday weeks signals outdoor leisure substitution and family outings, which spills over into nearby retail visits within one week and lifts RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week after a prior decline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -24.9 to -18.4 in t-1w before easing to -20.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: A week-on-week PARKS increase of more than 5 points is not followed by higher RETAIL_REC in the next week on repeated occurrences.

mechanism_narrative: Stable or improving GROCERY_PHARM alongside softer WORKPLACES indicates essential errands continue while discretionary work trips ease, redirecting time toward neighborhood shopping and raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved to 0.0 at t-0w while WORKPLACES improved from -37.3 to -21.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week average within 14 days when GROCERY_PHARM is nonnegative and WORKPLACES remains materially below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains below -35 for multiple weeks, retail access is still constrained enough that discretionary shopping does not recover, causing RETAIL_REC to stay flat or weaken over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -35 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -38.9 at t-1w and -31.6 at t-0w, after three earlier weeks below -33
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean within 28 days despite TRANSIT remaining below -35 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT marks a return of synchronized commuting, which increases retail footfall in adjacent commercial areas within four weeks and raises RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved at t-0w relative to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 28 days when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT trend upward together for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a holiday shopping regime, a short-lived improvement in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM signals local outing intensity and errand bundling, which converts into higher retail visits after two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises while GROCERY_PHARM is at or above 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not outperform its previous 28-day average within 14 days after PARKS rises and GROCERY_PHARM is nonnegative.
